title: Lesson 6: Resolving Issues Privately and Respectfully
summary: Protect client experience and dignity. Address the operational issue first, then discuss the disagreement privately using RESOLVE.

items.label: Focus
items.body: Private discussion, respectful language, facts versus assumptions and practical agreements

sections.title: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: A receptionist and therapist disagree about a client's appointment time. Instead of discussing the issue privately, they begin arguing at the reception desk. Their voices become louder.
A client waiting nearby hears the conversation. The client becomes uncomfortable and begins questioning whether the spa is professionally organised.
The disagreement has now affected more than the two employees. It has affected the client's experience.

Now imagine the employees handle the situation differently. The receptionist says: "I think there's a misunderstanding about the appointment. Let's confirm the client's booking first, then discuss the handover privately."
The immediate operational issue is addressed. The employees later discuss the communication problem away from clients.
Private and respectful conflict resolution protects employees' dignity and helps maintain a professional environment.

sections.title: 2. Why privacy matters
paragraphs: Privacy does not mean hiding misconduct or preventing appropriate documentation.
Serious concerns may require formal reporting or investigation.
list: Help employees concentrate on the actual issue.

sections.title: 3. Choose the right time and place
paragraphs: Poor timing: Confronting a colleague while she is attending to a client.
Better timing: Addressing any immediate operational concern, then discussing the disagreement at an appropriate moment.
list: In an environment where both people can communicate respectfully.
With an appropriate supervisor present when necessary.

sections.title: 4. Begin with the issue, not an accusation
paragraphs: Unhelpful opening: "You've been deliberately making my work difficult."
Better opening: "I'd like us to discuss the appointment handover because there have been some misunderstandings."
The second statement creates room for clarification.

sections.title: 5. Use respectful language
paragraphs: Employees should avoid insults, shouting, threats, mockery, sarcasm, exaggerated accusations and statements intended to embarrass.
list: "This affected my preparation, and I'd like us to prevent it happening again."
"What can we do differently going forward?"

sections.title: 6. Allow both people to speak
paragraphs: A conflict cannot be resolved fairly if only one person is allowed to explain.
Listening does not require agreeing with everything. It requires giving the other person a fair opportunity to be heard.

sections.title: 7. Separate facts from assumptions
paragraphs: An employee says: "You deliberately ignored my message." The colleague responds: "I didn't see the message until after my session." The original accusation may have been based on an assumption.
A better approach would be: "I sent a message about the schedule change but didn't receive a response. Did you see it?"
This invites clarification rather than confrontation.

items.label: R — Recognise the problem
items.body: Identify the specific issue that needs attention.

items.label: E — Engage privately when appropriate
items.body: Choose a suitable setting without unnecessary spectators.

items.label: S — Speak respectfully
items.body: Explain the concern without insults or accusations.

items.label: L — Look for solutions
items.body: Identify practical actions that address the problem.

items.label: V — Verify the agreement
items.body: Confirm responsibilities and expected next steps.

items.label: E — Evaluate the outcome
items.body: Follow up where necessary to ensure the issue has been resolved.

sections.title: 9. Agree on practical next steps
paragraphs: A conversation should not end with vague statements such as: "Let's just forget everything."
Where there is an operational issue, employees should identify what needs to change.

After discussing repeated appointment confusion, the receptionist and therapist agree that confirmed appointment changes will be communicated promptly, the assigned therapist will acknowledge receipt when practical, unclear bookings will be checked before the client arrives, and repeated problems will be raised with the supervisor.
The agreement focuses on preventing recurrence.

sections.title: 10. What if the other employee refuses to cooperate?
paragraphs: Not every disagreement can be resolved through a private conversation.
If the colleague refuses to communicate respectfully, becomes threatening or repeatedly ignores legitimate concerns, the employee should seek appropriate assistance.
Employees should not be pressured into private confrontation where they feel unsafe.

sections.title: 11. What if the conversation becomes heated?
paragraphs: A participant can say: "I want us to resolve this, but I don't think we're communicating productively right now. Can we pause and continue with the supervisor if necessary?"
Taking a brief pause can be useful when appropriate.
However, urgent operational or safety issues should still be addressed promptly.

sections.title: 12. Lesson 6 case study
paragraphs: A therapist and receptionist argue about a booking error in front of a waiting client.
Expected lesson: Resolve the immediate service issue, then address the interpersonal disagreement respectfully and through an appropriate process.
list: What should have been done immediately?
How could the employees discuss the issue privately?

sections.title: 13. Role-play: Private resolution
paragraphs: Divide participants into pairs. One employee plays a therapist. The other plays a receptionist.
The therapist believes an appointment change was not communicated properly. The receptionist believes the change was sent through the agreed channel.
list: Listen to the other person's explanation.
Agree on a practical next step.

remember: Not every workplace disagreement needs an audience. Address concerns at an appropriate time, protect confidentiality, listen fairly and concentrate on solutions that improve future cooperation.
